title: INDIA bloc rallies at Ramlila Maidan, demands CEC's exit; BJP marches on 1984 riots anniversary
dek: Opposition leaders from 19 parties, by the Congress's count, called for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to resign over the voter-roll revision. BJP president J P Nadda called the protest 'orchestrated drama'.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Leaders of the opposition INDIA bloc gathered at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan on Sunday for a "Chalo Delhi" rally against the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, demanding that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resign. Across the city, the BJP marched in West Delhi to mark the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, and party president J P Nadda called the opposition protest "a foolish, orchestrated drama".

Congress MP Manickam Tagore said 19 parties of the alliance had joined the protest, according to news agency ANI. Organisers made large claims about turnout that could not be independently checked, and police had deployed thousands of personnel across central Delhi. The rally is the biggest show of opposition strength on the voter-roll issue so far, two weeks before the Supreme Court resumes hearing petitions on the Election Commission's conduct.

## What happened

The march set off on Sunday morning towards Ramlila Maidan under the slogan "Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao" (Save the vote, save the nation). ANI's reports differ on the starting point, naming both the Constitution Club and the Minto Road-Connaught Place junction.

ANI named Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav, Trinamool Congress general secretary Abhishek Banerjee, Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren and Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy among the leaders taking part. ANI also listed Trinamool chairperson Mamata Banerjee, who had backed the rally on X last week; one ANI report wrongly described her as West Bengal's chief minister, a post she lost in May. Tamil Nadu ministers Thangam Thennarasu and Rajesh Kumar were also present.

Before the march, Mr Gandhi wrote on X: "Delhi, get ready! Save the Vote, Save the Nation." In the same post he called for paper ballots to replace electronic voting machines, ANI reported.

The speeches focused on Mr Kumar. "This Gyanesh Kumar has to answer: why is he not resigning?" Congress Rajya Sabha MP Rajeev Shukla said. Punjab Congress MP Amarinder Singh Raja Warring accused the government of "shielding" the CEC. Former Union minister Salman Khurshid said, "We do not want a single Indian to be left out," and called the rally part of an ongoing movement rather than a one-off event.

Samajwadi Party MP Neeraj Maurya claimed that "more than 13 crore" people had been struck off electoral rolls. The Declaration has not seen official data that supports that figure, and the Election Commission has not accepted the opposition's account of deletions.

CPI(M) MP John Brittas called it "a landmark protest" and alleged that volunteers had been stopped at Delhi's borders, with some taken off trains and detained. That claim had not been confirmed by Delhi Police at the time of writing.

## Crowd claims and security

Turnout figures came only from the organisers. Congress leader Ghulam Ahmad Mir told ANI that 8 to 10 lakh people had gathered; Mr Brittas also put the figure at 10 lakh. AICC general secretary K C Venugopal said "the entire Delhi is flooded with people". ANI's own report spoke of thousands of workers, students and civil society members arriving. None of these figures could be verified.

About 10,000 police and paramilitary personnel were deployed across central Delhi, with barricades and drone surveillance, ANI reported. Another ANI report said more than 4,000 were stationed around the ground itself, with prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, CCTV and facial-recognition cameras in use. Delhi Police had earlier set conditions for the rally, including that it end by 5 pm.

## The BJP's response

The BJP held a counter-march in West Delhi from the Hari Nagar bus depot to Tilak Nagar metro station to remember the victims of the 1984 riots, which began on November 1 that year after the assassination of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi. ANI named Union Minister Hardeep Singh Puri, Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, H S Phoolka, Manjinder Singh Sirsa and MP Bansuri Swaraj among those taking part, alongside members of the Sikh community. The party accused the Congress of holding a political rally on the anniversary of the violence.

Mr Nadda, a Union minister, said the protest was a "tactic instigated by foreign forces". He set out what he called Mr Gandhi's "anarchy model" in four stages: spreading lies, inciting anarchy on the streets, damaging the economy and destabilising an elected government "at the behest of foreign powers". He also said the choice of date was insensitive to Sikhs.

The Election Commission had not responded to Sunday's speeches by the time of writing. It has defended the SIR in the Supreme Court, saying in an affidavit last month that its decisions on the exercise were unanimous.

## Background

The SIR is a door-to-door re-verification of every voter on the rolls, which the Election Commission says is needed to remove dead, shifted and duplicate entries. Opposition parties say it has removed large numbers of genuine voters, especially the poor, migrants and minorities, and call this "vote chori" (vote theft). The Supreme Court is hearing several challenges; on Friday it asked the Commission to act on bulk complaints filed through Form 7 in Uttar Pradesh.

The rally was the second opposition event of the weekend. On Saturday, INDIA bloc MPs staged a symbolic "public impeachment" of Mr Kumar, with Mr Kharge listing six charges against him. The event has no legal force. Notices for a formal removal motion against the CEC were rejected in Parliament earlier this year; under the Constitution, a CEC can be removed only in the same way as a Supreme Court judge.

In Bengal, the issue has its own edge. About 16.1 lakh appeals have been filed against voters whom judicial officers had already found eligible in the state's SIR, and the Election Commission's special observer has said he was never officially told of them. The Trinamool, now in opposition in the state, has joined the national campaign against the Commission.

## What happens next

Opposition leaders said the protest would continue beyond Sunday but did not announce the next step. The Supreme Court bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant is due to hear the petitions on the Election Commission's functioning on November 17.

## Key numbers

- 19: INDIA bloc parties taking part, according to Congress MP Manickam Tagore
- 8-10 lakh: crowd claimed by Congress leader Ghulam Ahmad Mir (unverified)
- 10,000: police and paramilitary personnel across central Delhi, according to ANI
- November 17: next Supreme Court hearing on petitions about the Election Commission
